symptom: A flow parameter typed by a bare `Module.Name` naming an enumeration — `($Leg: "M"."ENUM_DeliveryLeg")` — made check report E009 'is an Object M.ENUM_DeliveryLeg, but the argument passed to it is an Enumeration' for every call passing a value; the stored parameter is an enumeration (describe: `enum M.ENUM_DeliveryLeg`) and mx check is clean.
cause: A bare Module.Name parses as ast.TypeEntity whatever it names. scriptFlowParams resolved the explicit Enumeration(...) form against the reader but typed every TypeEntity as KindObject, so a flow the script (re)declares with a bare enumeration type overlaid the catalog with Object.
fix: A TypeEntity reference the reader knows as an enumeration (and not as an entity) types the parameter KindEnumeration, as the writer resolves it.
insight: The same bare-name ambiguity was already handled one case below (TypeEnumeration with isEnum/KnowsEntity); when the parser cannot tell two kinds apart, every branch that types the AST must ask the model, not just the one written for the ambiguous spelling.
test: mdl/executor/typecheck_bare_enum_param_2259_test.go (controls: a string to the same parameter is still E009; a bare entity type still takes an object and refuses a primitive)
